source: Brooklyn Community Board 6 minutes at bkcb6.app/minutes, 2010 to 2026, motions and resolutions on street safety, transit and traffic. Text as recorded in the minutes. Votes are as recorded; committee minutes often record the outcome without a count.

positions.title: Grand Army Plaza improvements approved
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve the Department of Transportation’s planned improvements to the Grand Army Plaza as presented at the committee’s April 29, 2010 meeting.

positions.title: Pedestrian safety plan for Atlantic Avenue, Columbia Street and Furman Street at Pier 6
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation that the Department of Transportation come up with a plan to improve pedestrian safety in the Atlantic Avenue/Columbia Street/Furman Street area as an approach to Pier 6 given the significant increase in pedestrian activity attracted to the newly opened Brooklyn Bridge Park facilities at Pier 6. Board Member Ben Atkins spoke in favor of the motion stating that we should do whatever we can to encourage DOT to improve pedestrian safety in the area. 5 Board Member Constance Molinari asked if DOT could make the “No Right Turn on Red’ sign at the corner of Columbia Street and Atlantic Avenue more prominent by adding lights. Chairperson Bashner stated that we could add it to the letter.

positions.title: Union Street lane markings and No Standing hours at Plaza Street West
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve the Department of Transportation’s plan to place lane markings on Union Street for a second lane eastbound at Plaza Street West and exchange "No Standing" from 7-10am and 4-7pm, Monday through Friday to “No Parking”, 7am-10pm everyday on the south curb of Union Street between 8th Avenue and PPW/GAP. Board Member Daniel Kummer asked if they were going to change the parking lane into a driving lane. Transportation Co-Chairperson Burzio stated yes during the posted hours. Board Member Elizabeth Shipley stated that this will not solve the problem of congestion or bottlenecking on 8th Avenue, but it is a start. Board Member Gary Reilly stated that this is part of the larger redesign of Grand Army Plaza. Board Member Constance Molinari asked why the hours went to 10pm. Chairperson Bashner stated that DOT wanted to go to midnight but after talking with the committee, they compromised at 10pm. Board Member Elly Spicer asked if it would be two travel lanes. Transportation Co-Chairperson Miskel stated yes in the eastbound direction. Board Member Kummer asked if DOT tried to change the traffic light pattern to improve the situation. Transportation Co-Chairperson Miskel stated yes, but it did not work and this is the best solution they could come up with at this time. Board Member Monique Verret asked if the Board could ask MTA not to allow the group

positions.title: ParkSMART peak-rate parking meters on Park Slope corridors
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to support the continuation of the ParkSMART parking meter peak rate of $0.50 per 20 minutes coupled with the maximum 1-hour parking regulation for the parking meters in Park Slope along 5th and 7th Avenues, including spur meters, and along 9th Street. Board Member Levine would like it stated that we are only talking about existing spur meters on 9 th Street. Chairperson Bashner affirmed. 8 Amendment: by Board Member Nica Lalli, seconded by Board Member Robert Levine; To ask DOT to come up with a plan to address two-wheeled motorized vehicles in the ParkSMART parking meter program. AMENDMENT PASSED UNANIMOUSLY TIME: 7:55 P.M.

positions.title: 4th Street cul-de-sac restricted to school and park use (Play Street)
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to support a proposal to restrict vehicular usage of the 4th Street cul-de-sac (west of 5th Avenue) in favor of expanded school use (i.e.; Play Street) and community use by park users, residents and merchants. Board Member Robert Levine asked if teachers would lose parking. Transportation Co-Chairperson Stephen Burzio stated that the teachers’ spaces have already been reallocated and that no spaces were lost. Board Member Elly Spicer asked is this play street option a restricted time so that no parking spaces will be lost because there is parking there now and taking all parking there is not fair to the community and she would be opposed to that. Transportation Co-Chairperson Stephen Burzio stated that there would be parking after 5pm. Board Member Constance Molinari spoke in favor of the motion stating that we should remove parking in favor of the children. Board Member Richard Bashner asked if parking will be available in the evenings and on weekends. Transportation Co-Chairperson Stephen Burzio stated yes. Board Member Nica Lalli spoke in favor of the motion stating that the cul-de-sac is used by ambulances to sit and idle and we should use the space as a play area for children. Board Member Robert Levine asked if the farmer’s market would be able to continue to use the cul-de-sac on the weekend. Transportation Co-Chairperson Stephen Burzio state

positions.title: Prospect Park West bike lane modifications approved, with conditions
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve the Department of Transportation’s proposed modifications to the Prospect Park West bike lanes with the following conditions: 1. Brooklyn CB6 approves the concept to build out raised pedestrian safety islands on PPW, subject to the following conditions: (a) Brooklyn CB6 strongly believes that DOT should not complete this work using ordinary in-house street improvement resources, but should instead treat it as a capital project with design and material needs that flow from the historic and special character of its environs. In this connection, DOT should work with the Department of Parks & Recreation, the Prospect Park Alliance, the Park Slope Civic Council and our district office to develop an appropriate design, for public review, that will result in islands and landscaping treatments that are in keeping with the historic character of PPW and the design of the eastside sidewalk, including, but not limited to, complementary materials and alternatives to the unsightly plastic delineators affixed to the current grade-level islands. We believe it would be appropriate to begin the preliminary design process now. (b) DOT should, if possible, expand the width of the islands into the buffer zone between the bike and parking lanes in order to enhance pedestrian visibility and ease of crossing the lanes, while simultaneously reducing the length of

positions.title: Interagency rules-of-the-road education for cyclists, drivers and pedestrians on Prospect Park West
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to support and encourage an interagency approach to educating the community (bicyclist, motorist and pedestrians) about the rules of the road, particularly as they pertain to the bike lanes on Prospect Park West.

positions.title: Interim DOT changes at the Atlantic Avenue entrance to Brooklyn Bridge Park approved; permanent fix demanded
positions.text: Motion by Jerry Armer, seconded by Madelaine Murphy: Though we thank DOT for these interim improvements, they are far from the permanent solutions needed at the Atlantic Avenue entrance to Brooklyn Bridge Park. We approve the DOT proposal as an interim step.

positions.title: Pedestrian ramps and granite curbs with the Prospect Park West median islands
positions.text: by Board Member Richard Bashner, seconded by Board Member Glenn Kelly; Recommendation that the Department of Transportation include paired pedestrian ramp installations as necessary on all sidewalks of Prospect Park West as part of the construction of the raised median islands as well as the inclusion of granite curbs. Board Member asked what the rule was in regards to the placement of pedestrian ramps when there is no crosswalk. District Manager Hammerman explained that pedestrian ramps are required to be installed where there are traffic control devices. Crosswalks are not traffic control devices. A traffic control device would be a traffic signal, Stop sign or some other element that controls traffic. Board Member Atkins made a friendly amendment not to move pedestrian cross signals. Board Member Richard Bashner did not except the friendly amendment. Amendment: by Board Member James Bernard, seconded by Board Member Benjamin Atkins; To stipulate that the Department of Transportation not move the pedestrian cross signals. Board Member Mark Shames spoke in favor of the motion stating that you are not going to be able to change the behavior of people by move the signals, so why do it. Board Member Levine spoke in favor of the motion. Board Member Bashner stated that we are mixing issues a little bit. He supported adding signal for bicyclist but DOT rejected it. When you see a g

positions.title: Red Hook Transit Access and Mobility Improvements supported
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to support the improvements called for in the Department of Transportation’s Red Hook Transit Access and Mobility Improvements presentation. Board Member Lou Sones was disappointed that Richards Street between Verona and Hamilton Avenue making it a two way street again was not included in the improvements.

positions.title: Two-way bike lane on Plaza Street at Grand Army Plaza, conditional approval
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to conditionally approve the Department of Transportation’s proposed installation of a two- way Class II bicycle lane on Plaza Street at the Grand Army Plaza as a step toward a Class I bicycle lane (not parking-protected) on the conditions (1) that the department consider further how to separate the bike lanes from the moving traffic lane, (2) that within 6 months the department perform a before and after analysis of safety at the circle considering accidents and/or injuries by motorists, cyclists and pedestrians as well as suggestions for safety improvements, (3) that the department further consider banning a left turn by motorists from Plaza Street West onto the Union Street approach into the Grand Army Plaza; and (4) that the department explore the possibility of installing crosswalks at the intersections of Lincoln and Berkeley Places at Plaza Street West. Amendment: by Board Member Richard Bashner, seconded by Board Member Nica Lalli; To strike the third condition from the motion regarding the banning of the left turn as it is not clear that limiting Plaza Street residents’ mobility is in our interest, nor is it clear that it is in fact a left turn and not simply an extension of the circular arc of the roadway. AMENDMENT PASSED TIME: 9:30 P.M. Discussion continued on the main motion as amended. Chairperson Kummer added that we will include our

positions.title: Bike corral at 5th Avenue and Park Place
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install an on-street bicycle parking facility at the northeast corner 5th Avenue and Park Place.

positions.title: 3rd Street bike lane between 3rd and 4th Avenues
positions.text: by Committee; 11 Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install an eastbound and westbound bicycle lane on one block of 3rd Street between 3rd and 4th Avenues to extend and connect pre- existing bicycle lanes on 3rd Street (between Smith Street-3rd Avenue and between 4th Avenue-Prospect Park West.

positions.title: Bartel-Pritchard Square pedestrian safety improvements
positions.text: by Board Member Nica Lalli, seconded by Board Member Ben Solotaire; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation for various pedestrian safety improvements at the Bartel-Pritchard Square traffic circle. Board Member Rosemary Graham asked what were the reasons for the changes. Transportation Committee Chairperson Miskel stated Pedestrian Safety Enhancements. Board Member Nica Lalli spoke in favor of the

positions.title: 14th Street bike lane from Prospect Park West
positions.text: by Board Member Ben Solotaire, seconded by Board Member Nica Lalli; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install an eastbound bicycle lane along 14th Street between Prospect Park West and 3rd Avenue and a westbound bicycle lane along 15th Street between Bartel-Pritchard Square and 3rd Avenue with the condition that on-street bicycle parking in front of the YMCA Armory take a full 2 spots. Board Member Robert Levine asked why when DOT created the bike lanes on 9th Street and we asked for 15th Street they said no. But now it is ok, what has changed? Transportation Committee Co-Chairperson Miskel stated he did not know. Board Member Roger Rigolli stated that DOT is installing a lot of bike lanes putting individuals in harm’s way. He asked if we could get the stats on accident and fatality rates. Board Member Richard Bashner spoke in favor of the motion stating that bicyclist have a legal right to be on the road and the lanes make it safer and it lets everyone know where they should be. Board Member Elizabeth Shipley spoke in favor of the motion stating that bike lanes make the street safer and it encourages others to ride on them as well. Board Member Judith Thompson spoke in favor of the motion asking what type of lanes will be installed. Transportation Committee Chairperson Miskel stated mostly Class 2 painted lanes.

positions.title: Hicks Street corridor traffic safety measures
positions.text: by Board Member Ben Solotaire, seconded by Board Member Nica Lalli; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation for various traffic safety measures being pursued by the department in the Hicks Street corridor as a follow-up to the BQE Trench Enhancement Study with the condition that DOT install countdown timers at each pedestrian crossing and report back with an update on the possibility to include extra width for pedestrian visibility on the BQE side of the street. 11 Board Member Judith Thompson spoke in favor of the motion.

positions.title: Boerum Hill Neighborhood Slow Zone designated
positions.text: by Board Member Nica Lalli, seconded by Board Member Ben Solotaire; Recommendation to approve a proposal to designate the Boerum Hill Neighborhood Slow Zone, the area bounded by Atlantic Avenue, Smith Street, Union Street and 3rd Avenue with the condition that we encourage DOT to provide “greening” measures at the gateways/entrances to the zone.

positions.title: Atlantic Basin and Red Hook Greenway approved
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve the implementation of the Department of Transportation's Atlantic Basin/Red Hook Greenway project concepts.

positions.title: Red Hook one-way conversions: Conover, Beard and Reed Streets, study requested
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to request that the Department of Transportation further study and obtain community input for the potential conversions of: 1. Conover Street to one-way northbound from Beard Street to Sullivan Street. 2. Beard Street to one-way westbound from Van Brunt Street to Conover Street. 3. Reed Street to one-way eastbound from Conover Street to Van Brunt Street. Board Member Greg O’Connell Jr. stated that DOT should also include the businesses in on the discussions. Chairperson Kummer stated that it would be added to the request. Board Member Roger Rigolli is against the changes because it would be confusing to truckers with all the changes and the changing of direction for truckers would increase dramatically. Board Member Greg O’Connell Jr. stated that the change needs to happen to make it safer for trucks to change direction.

positions.title: Bike corral at 787 Union Street
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a new on- street bicycle parking facilities (bike corral) in front of 787 Union Street (between 5th/6th Avenues). Board Member Rosemary Graham asked if there would be any parking impact. Public Safety Committee Chairperson Sayar Lonial stated no. Board Member Lou Sones spoke in favor of the motion.

positions.title: Bike corral at 153 Columbia Street
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a new on- street bicycle parking facilities (bike corral) in front of 153 Columbia Street (between Kane/Degraw Streets). positions.title: Union Street and Sackett Street bike lanes in Carroll Gardens and Red Hook
positions.text: by Board Member Peter Fleming, seconded by Board Member Elizabeth Shipley; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a new pair of bicycle lanes on Union Street and Sackett Street between Van Brunt Street and 3rd Avenue Board Member Roger Rigolli is concerned with the safety of bicyclist in relation to truck traffic as they get closer to Van Brunt Street. Board Member Daniel Kummer stated that he has some reservations in regards to adding a bike lane on Union Street between Hicks and Henry Street where the 76th Police Precinct has angle parking may be a safety concern as it relates to enough space for cars and bikes. Friendly Amendment: by Board Member Daniel Kummer, accepted by Board Member Peter Fleming, Recommendation to ask DOT to reevaluate the class 1 bike lanes on Union Street between Henry and Hicks streets possibly making them to Class 2 or Class 3 lanes. Discussion on original motion as amended continued.

positions.title: Bike corral at 153 Columbia Street deferred
positions.text: by Board Member Daniel Kummer, accepted by Board Member Roger Rigolli, Recommendation to ask DOT to defer the bike corral until such time as there’s a greater demonstrated need and/or to potentially fold this proposal into the planning for the park space that will hopefully be installed across from this location. Board Member Daniel Kummer stated that while he was inspecting the block for the possible bike corral he did observe 7 bike racks and 5 of them were unused. There are also several unused bike racks on adjoining blocks. At this time he does not see a need to justify the removing of parking to add a bike corral. There are residential buildings, ball fields, restaurants, and a mental health facility/home on or in the immediate vicinity in which visitors and residents will need the scarce parking, and to take away any parking even if it is one space would be detrimental to the area. It also sets a bad precedent, particularly as we are on the cusp of dealing with the whole 5 issue of the siting of the bike share locations to simply grant a group’s request to remove a parking space in front of its office. It’s not to take away at all from the excellent work that the Brooklyn Greenway Initiative has done, but having a bike corral in front of their office is not critical to their mission. Board Member Elizabeth Shipley asked if this proposal was something DOT came up with or w

positions.title: 4th Avenue redesign, Atlantic Avenue to 15th Street: committee motion to approve with conditions
positions.text: by Committee; 9 Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to redesign 4th Avenue traffic corridor (between Atlantic Avenue and 15th Streets) with the following condition that DOT come back to the committee with a full layout of bike corrals, loading zones, and metered parking, etc. Board Member Elizabeth Shipley asked if anyone brought up the fact that there were a lot of eastbound “no turns” from 4th Avenue. Transportation/Public Safety Committee Co-Chair Thomas Miskel stated yes. Board Member Robert Levine stated that since there is a school on 5th Street DOT should install a traffic light there. Board Member Jeff Strabone asked if the Chair could characterize the sentiments of the 5th Street residents. Transportation/Public Safety Committee Co-Chair Thomas Miskel stated that they were totally against the no left turn especially at 3rd street. It would bring more vehicles especially trucks on their block causing a dangerous situation for pedestrians specifically children. Board Member Suzanne Turet stated that 5th Street is not a great block to divert traffic to. 3rd Street is much wider and can handle the traffic. Board Member Gary Reilly stated that DOT had a number of meetings where a number of organizations and residents came out and gave there input. The one thing that came out was that 4th Avenue in its current condition was dangerous and

positions.title: 4th Avenue redesign disapproved (June 2013)
positions.text: by Board Member James Bernard, seconded by Board Member Peter Fleming; Recommendation to disapprove a proposal by the Department of Transportation to redesign 4th Avenue traffic corridor (between Atlantic Avenue and 15th Streets). Board Member Gary Reilly stated that before you commit to a motion as extreme as this one is you must think long and hard about what you know about the proposal before saying that it should not be put in. We must bear in mind the safety issues and the input of the hundreds of people from the neighborhood before we discard the proposal. Board Member James Bernard stated that he thinks it is enough to vote no based on the no turning lanes on 3rd and 9th Streets. If we don’t say affirmly no, DOT will interpret this as us not having a position on this proposal. Board Member Jeff Strabone asked if someone could explain all of the elements in the proposal. Chairperson Kummer gave a brief explanation of the elements. Board Member Peter Fleming stated that he lives on 4th Avenue and Union Street and he does not drive his car that much. On many days traffic is always backed up to 9th Street and with these changes traffic especially if there is one less lane traffic will be backed up to 15th Street. These changes will not discourage outside drivers from using 4th Avenue it will only punish the ones who live in the area by making us drive in circles to find park

positions.title: Red Hook one-way conversions approved by the Executive Committee
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal to convert Conover Street (Beard/Sullivan Sts) to one-way northbound, Beard Street (Conover/Van Brunt Sts) to one-way westbound, and Reed Street (Conover/Van Brunt Sts) to one-way eastbound.

positions.title: 4th Avenue redesign approved with conditions (July 2013)
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to redesign 4th Avenue traffic corridor (between Atlantic Avenue and 15th Streets) with the following conditions: 1) That the department return to the Community Board with specific proposal(s) to review before any other changes are implemented for 4th Avenue, including but not limited to the addition of loading zones, bicycle corrals, bicycle lanes, metered parking, etc.; 2) That the prohibited southbound left-turns be further reviewed with an eye toward including additional signage and/or other strategies that would minimize the impact of turning traffic that is displaced specifically to 5`h and/or 10`h Streets; 3) That the department return to the Community Board with an evaluative report one-year after the project implementation; 2 4) That the department collects new traffic and pedestrian counts in the vicinity of the Whole Foods Market at 3rd Avenue and 3rd Street, within 6 to 12 months after the store opens; and, 5) That the department further review and develop plans to beautify the 4th Avenue corridor beyond the limited plantings suggested in the revised plan. Board Member Judith Thompson stated that she has driven on 4th Avenue in Sunset Park and was frustrated because of the painted markings on the ground. DOT should “build up” with cement where the markings are as well as including

positions.title: North Flatbush Avenue pedestrian improvements capital design
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve the Department of Transportation’s designs for the North Flatbush Avenue Pedestrian Improvements Capital project HWK300-01 with the following condition that DOT look at the potential of increasing the use of permeable surfaces and inclusion of more bicycle racks, including Citi Bikes. Board Member Ariel Krasnow asked if there would be any budget overlap with DEP in regards to the installation of bioswells. Transportation/Public Safety Chair Thomas Miskel stated no because they are limited by the capital budget.

positions.title: Bond Street bike lane, conditional approval
positions.text: by Board Member Judith Thompson, seconded by Board Member Sayar Lonial; Recommendation to conditionally approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation (DOT) to install a new bicycle lane on Bond Street between 3rd Street and Schermerhorn Street. The new bike lane would be a Class III shared lane between 3rd-Douglass, a Class II bike lane 10 between Douglass-Wyckoff and a Class III shared lane between Wyckoff-Schermerhorn. The condition would require DOT to resurface Bond Street prior to the new bike lane installation. Board Member Mark Shames stated that he is not against bike lanes but he is fed up with the lack of enforcement by the Police and the lack of respect from bicyclists. Board Member Roger Rigolli stated that DOT needs to table the entire new bicycle lane until they fix the infrastructure of the streets, i.e. potholes, depressions, etc. Board Member John Heyer stated that he does not think it is a safe idea to install a shared bike lane between 3rd and Douglass streets because a number of trucks are on Bond Street and inviting bicyclists to use it may not be the best idea.

positions.title: Bike corral at 365 5th Avenue
positions.text: by Board Member Lou Sones, seconded by Board Member Elizabeth Shipley; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a new bicycle parking facility (bike corral) in front of 365 Van Brunt Street (southeast corner of Van Brunt/Dikeman Streets). Board Member Elly Spicer asked why DOT has to take parking away. Did they try a parking neutral solution? Transportation Co-Chair Sayar Lonial stated that that issue did not come up in the committee meeting. Board Member Roger Rigolli stated that DOT needs to halt these things and focus on making our streets safer by fixing the roadway surfaces, i.e. potholes, depressions, etc. Board Member Sister Rosanna Cervone stated that this installation would be dangerous because Van Brunt Street is a truck route. Board Member Lou Sones spoke in favor of the motion stating that every corner on Van Brunt Street there is a problem with daylighting and this installation will help with visibility and slow traffic down. Board Member Elizabeth Shipley spoke in favor of the motion stating that along this strip of Van Brunt it is harder to park a bike than it is to park a car.

positions.title: State bill lowering the citywide speed limit to 25 mph supported (Vision Zero)
positions.text: by Board Member Richard Bashner, seconded by Board Member Lou Sones; Recommendation to support New York State Assembly Bill A.8478-A and Senate Bill S.6496-A respectively, an act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to reducing the speed limit in the city of New York to twenty miles per hour. Chairperson Daniel Kummer relinquished the Chair to 1st Vice Chairperson Thomas Miskel for the Transportation & Public Safety Committee Report. Board Member Kummer spoke in favor of the motion stating that we have to get motorists to slow down because there have been too many tragedies in our city. Secondly, we need to take back our streets and reduce this epidemic of speeding traffic and traffic-related accidents and deaths. Board Member Dolly Williams asked what the enforcement mechanism would be. Public Safety Chair Matthew Silverman stated that enforcement would not change. Board Member Lou Sones spoke in favor of the motion stating that recently a boy was fatally killed by a motorist in Red Hook on a section that does not have a stop sign or traffic light for 4 blocks. He also stated that there is a dangerous situation occurring in Red Hook with drag racing. Board Member Richard Bashner spoke in favor of the motion stating that enough kids have died and we have to get the cars to slow down. Board Member Gary Reilly spoke

positions.title: Bike corral on Bergen Street
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a new on-street bicycle parking facility (bike corral) on Bergen Street (between 6th/Carlton Avenues), adjacent to the NYPD/78th Precinct at 65 6th Avenue.

positions.title: Gowanus Greenway Connector on Hamilton Avenue
positions.text: by Board Member Jerry Armer, seconded by Board Member Glenn Kelly; Recommendation to approve the Department of Transportation’s proposed Gowanus Greenway Connector on Hamilton Avenue between Smith Street and 29th Street as presented and also to encourage the expedited implementation of the Gowanus part of the Brooklyn Waterway Greenway Initiative. Board Member Roger Rigolli spoke out against the motion stating that he can’t believe that DOT would want to put a bike lane on Hamilton Avenue. He also would want DOT to fix the roadway in and around this area before installing the connector. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure stated that this will be a protected bike path and that DOT will be making a full analysis of the entire stretch of roadway focusing on sewer issues. Board Member Richard Bashner stated that DOT would not eliminate any lanes and will make it safer for bicyclists. 5 Board Member Benjamin Solotaire spoke in favor of the motion stating that it will be safer for bicyclists. Board Member Daniel Kummer asked if DOT was going to narrow the roadway. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure stated that they will be narrowing the driving lanes from 12ft to 11ft and DOT does not believe this will have any adverse effects on traffic.

positions.title: Move NY Fair Tolling plan supported
positions.text: by Committee; Recommendation to support the Fair Tolling and Transportation Reinvestment Plan, as proposed by Move NY. Board Member Bob Levine asked how they came up with 90% of Brooklyn drivers will pay the same or lower tolls. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure explained that the plan states that 94% of Brooklyn automotive trips would be paying the same toll or lower because most of the trips would not be going over the East River bridges. Board Member Judith Thompson spoke out against the motion stating it is unfair to people who live in the outer boroughs who drive their cars because they are underserved by mass transportation, as well as anyone who has a doctor in Manhattan. We’re one city and we should not have to pay a tax to go over a bridge. It’s a boondoggle for a bloated agency and she does not think that it is going to end up helping people in Brooklyn because we are going to be paying taxes and it prevents people from moving freely throughout the boroughs. Board Member Hildegaard Link spoke out against the motion stating that it is not a positive thing for Brooklyn drivers. This will isolate Brooklyn and create little countries as well as make it a struggle to go to Manhattan like the residents of Staten Island. Board Member Ellie Spicer spoke out against the motion. She takes offense at the plan claiming that it will save Brooklynites money. Also, we are a city

positions.title: Bike corral at 248 5th Avenue
positions.text: by Board Member Jerry Armer, seconded by Board Member Hildegaard Link; Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to install a bicycle parking facility (bike corral) in front of 248 5th Avenue (northwest corner 5th Avenue/Carroll Street). Board Member Suzanne Turet asked if DOT is required to post notices for the proposed bike corral in the neighborhood. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure stated no. Board Member Daniel Kummer asked if we knew about the adequacy of bike parking on the block. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure stated that all of the bike racks on the block are fully occupied. Board Member Pauline Blake stated that losing a parking space will be detrimental to the block. Board Member Sayar Lonial asked if the other bike corral in the neighborhood is well used. Transportation Co- Chair Eric McClure stated yes. Board Member Suzanne Turet spoke out against the motion stating that it is very difficult to find parking on Carroll and President Streets. Board Member Elly Spicer spoke out against the motion stating that she is opposed to eliminating a parking space for the corral.

positions.title: 4th Avenue median reconstruction, preliminary design
positions.text: by Board Member Jerry Armer, seconded by Board Member Glen Kelly; Recommendation to approve the preliminary design concepts proposed by the Department of Transportation for the 4th Avenue Median Reconstruction project (between 8th-15th Streets). . Board Member Judith Thompson asked how/why DOT chose those streets and no other ones in the district. Transportation Co-Chair Eric McClure stated that he believed that it was based on crash incidents. District Manager Hammerman stated that DOT wanted to include the 9th Street intersection in it and so had to start on 8th Street. There is a possibility of them extending the reconstruction project along 4 th Avenue in the second phase of funding. 9

positions.title: Commerce Street converted to one-way in Red Hook
positions.text: Recommendation to approve a proposal by the Department of Transportation to convert Commerce Street from Van Brunt Street to Imlay Street to a one-way operation from two-way operation, and a proposal to reverse the direction of Verona Street from Imlay Street to Van Brunt Street.

positions.title: NYC Transit asked for ADA plans at 7th Avenue, Smith-9th, Grand Army Plaza and 4th Avenue stations
positions.text: Recommendation to request that NYC Transit provide the Community Board with handicapped- accessible plans for the 7th Avenue, Smith-9th Street, Grand Army Plaza and 4th Avenue subway stations within one year.

positions.title: Valentino Pier approaches: pedestrian and bicycle safety design
positions.text: As amended, recommendation anticipated on the preliminary designs for Valentino Pier approaches (Capital Project #HWK1048J), a project is to improve the public realm, enhancing pedestrian and bicycle safety, and have sustainable elements to capture stormwater along the street segments of Ferris Street (between King/Van Dyke Streets) and Beard Street (between Otsego/Conover Streets) in Red Hook. 6

positions.title: Citi Bike docking station plan for the district
positions.text: Recommendation anticipated on the Department of Transportation's proposed CitiBike bike share docking stations deployment plan for the CB6 district.

positions.title: Bond Street bike lane upgrade
positions.text: Motion to approve the Department of Transportation’s proposal to upgrade the existing Bond Street bike lane between Douglass and 3rd Streets in the district. Board Member Paul Basile asked how many businesses curb cuts were impacted by the proposal. Committee Co-Chair McClure said we can ask DOT. Board Member Joe Ann Brown asked if there was any way to effectively separate bicycles and trucks. Board Member Paul Basile said this kind of treatment increases liability for businesses that use the space in front of their building for loading and unloading. Board Member Suzanne Turet stated that bicyclists need to make things safer for pedestrians, not more hazardous.

positions.title: Bike corral at 341 5th Avenue tabled
positions.text: By Board Member Jerry Armer; seconded by Board Member Mark Shames. To table the Department of Transportation’s proposal for a new bike corral at 341 5th Avenue due to their not adhering to the committee’s request for letters of approval from surrounding businesses.

positions.title: Mayor and DOT asked for safety measures on the 9th Street corridor
positions.text: By Board Member Eric McClure; seconded by Board Member Peter Fleming To communicate to the Office of the Mayor and the NYC Department of Transportation a request to analyze and implement necessary safety measures along the Ninth Street corridor in Park Slope. Discussion ensued, with various Board members requesting that various specifics be either added to or subtracted from the request. Some wished to see specific demands on truck traffic; others pointed out the economic importance of truck traffic. After several minutes of back and forth, parties agreed that the original intent of the motion was to express a specific demand on the relevant government agencies, and that further considerations could be taken up by the Transportation & Public Safety committee in future meetings. 2 The question was called by Board Member Jerry Armer.

positions.title: Court Street redesign supported, with hardened daylighting, concrete curbs, 15 to 20 mph, LPIs and loading zones
positions.text: Jerry 2nd: Madeline The transportation committee of Community Board 6 thanks DOT for its plan for Court Street. We support the project and urge DOT to put the new design into effect this summer. Additionally, we ask that DOT include additional improvements: - The installation of hard infrastructure (bike corrals, planters, boulders) on pedestrian islands to prevent illegal parking, blocked crosswalks and blocked sightlines. - Additional daylighting on side streets with hard infrastructure. - Harder bike lane barriers such as low concrete curbs instead of plastic Kwik Curbs. - A lower speed limit of 15 - 20 mph on the corridor in accordance with Sammy's Law. - Leading Pedestrian Intervals (LPI's) at all intersections where they don't already exist. - Extended loading zone hours until at least 8 PM to accommodate Amazon, FedEx, UPS and other later deliveries. We also ask that: - DOT follow up with NYPD for additional parking enforcement in the period immediately post installation. - DOT study the potential for speed cushions on Court Street after project installation. - DOT study and come back to the committee with a plan for a northbound projected bike lane on Clinton Street. 4. positions.title: End criminal summonses for cyclists; regulate app companies to make delivery workers employees
positions.text: Motion to approve the the plan as presented with the urging that it be installed as quickly as possible. A recommendation: The Transportation Committee of Community Board 6 calls on Mayor Adams and NYPD Commissioner Tisch to end the crackdown on cyclists. Issuing criminal summonses to cyclists, for infractions that would earn motorists a mere traffic ticket, is not only unfair, but risks exposing the largely immigrant delivery cyclist workforce to law enforcement in ways that could result in deportation without due process. At a time when immigrants are under threat from the federal government and due process rights are being denied, the police should not target essential workers and our fellow New Yorkers, no matter when they arrived in the city. While not condoning illegal or dangerous behavior, we do not believe that such infractions should be subject to criminal summonses. In addition to calling on the city to end this practice, we ask that the mayor work with the City Council to advance existing proposals to regulate app companies so that they are forced to classify delivery cyclists not as independent contractors but as employees with full benefits and standardized, legal equipment and vehicles for doing their jobs.

positions.title: District-wide 20 MPH slow zone under Sammy’s Law, with signal retiming and camera enforcement; citywide 20 mph
positions.text: C. The Transportation, Parks & Public Infrastructure Resolution to Introduce a District-Wide 20 MPH Slow Zone Tony Melone presented the following resolution: Recognizing CB6’s commitment to safer streets and support for Sammy’s Law, we recommend that NYC DOT institute a district-wide 20 MPH slow zone on all applicable streets, and adjust signal timing to reflect the new limit, with camera enforcement. We also call for the adoption of a citywide speed limit of 20mph on all applicable streets. Tony explained that Safe Streets and Make McGuinness Safe were presented at the last committee meeting. He explained that the district-wide speed limit would apply only to streets with no more than two lanes in one direction, and that similar motions have been passed by Brooklyn Community Board 1 and Queens Community Board 2. The committee passed the resolution unanimously with one abstention for cause. Marc Torrence noted that while the reduction from 25 MPH to 20 MPH seems small, it significantly improves survivability in crashes. Tony noted that enforcement typically begins 10 MPH over the limit, meaning tickets would start at 30 MPH. The resolution passed unanimously, with Pauline Blake abstaining. positions.title: Parking enforcement returned to NYC DOT
positions.text: B. The Transportation, Parks & Public Infrastructure Resolution to Shift Traffic Enforcement Responsibilities to NYCDOT Tony Melone presented the following resolution: BKCB6 supports returning parking enforcement to the NYC Department of Transportation where it was before 1996, so that it can get the attention it needs and allow NYPD to focus on crime reduction. BKCB6 asks our elected officials to support this work through legislation that would make it a possibility. The motion was proposed by Jerry Armer and passed unanimously at the most recent committee meeting, with quorum. It has also been recommended as part of the board’s District Needs assessment. Laura Osorio asked whether NYCDOT has a position on this transfer of responsibility, and Jerry reiterated that a decision like this lies with elected officials and not with the agencies responsible for implementation. Tony explained that one advantage of this change would be that NYCDOT has additional tools to resolve parking issues not at NYPD’s disposal, such as installing granite blocks in no parking zones. Reema noted that Manhattan Community Board 6 has passed a similar resolution inspired by ours. The motion passed unanimously, with Pauline Blake abstaining and Leroy Branch abstaining for cause.

positions.title: Hamilton Avenue changes approved with HAWK signals at midblock crossings; street direction changes sent back for study
positions.text: Motion to approve all changes presented by DOT on both sides of Hamilton Avenue, with the addition of HAWK signals at the midblock crossings. Interventions proposed by DOT included street direction changes for Woodhull and Rapelye Streets, new crosswalks across Hamilton Avenue, lane reductions on Hamilton Avenue and Woodhull Street, and traffic delineators to prevent illegal right turns from Hamilton Avenue. The motion, modified to approve the changes presented by DOT with further study on the street direction changes with the participation of residents of the neighborhood, passed unanimously.
